title: Chimichurri Steak
subtitle: Seared sirloin with herbed chimichurri sauce
excerpt: Pan-seared sirloin steaks served with a sharp, herby chimichurri made from parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, and chilli. The sauce is bright and punchy against the richness of the beef.
sourceNotes: Chimichurri is a herb sauce from Argentina, where it is traditionally served alongside grilled meats. The name's origin is debated, with some suggesting it derives from Basque or Moorish words carried to South America by immigrants. It has become one of the defining sauces of Argentine asado culture.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Chimichurri can be made up to 24 hours ahead. The flavour deepens as it sits.

content.text: Bring the steaks to room temperature for 20 minutes before cooking. A cold steak will cook unevenly in the pan.

Make the chimichurri. Mix the chopped parsley, garlic, olive oil, red wine vinegar, chilli flakes, and dried oregano in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to let the flavours develop while you cook the steaks.
Pat the steaks dry with kitchen paper and season generously on both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat the frying pan over very high heat until it is smoking. Add a small splash of oil, then add the steaks one or two at a time without crowding the pan. Sear for 2 to 3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium.
Rest the steaks on a warm plate for 5 minutes before slicing. Serve topped with chimichurri.

items.symptom: Steak is grey and steamed rather than seared
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or steaks were wet
items.fix: Pat steaks dry and use a very hot pan.

items.cause: Too much vinegar for the amount of oil
items.fix: Add more oil a spoonful at a time until balanced.
Rest steak for at least 5 minutes before cutting.
